question.prompt:
As shown in the figure, a triangular corner with side lengths \(DB=EB=1\) is cut from equilateral triangle \(ABC\) of side length \(3.\) The perimeter of the remaining quadrilateral \(ADEC\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1987_AMC_12_Q02_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The only new side of the remaining quadrilateral is \(DE\), so first find its length. Since \(ABC\) is equilateral and \(D\) and \(E\) lie on \(AB\) and \(CB\), respectively, \(\angle DBE=60^\circ\). Also, \(BD=BE=1\). An isosceles triangle with a \(60^\circ\) vertex angle is equilateral, so \(DE=1\).

The two shortened sides have lengths
\[
AD=3-1=2,\qquad EC=3-1=2.
\]
Adding the four sides along the boundary of \(ADEC\) gives
\[
AD+DE+EC+CA=2+1+2+3=8.
\]
The perimeter is \(\boxed{8}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Recognize the equilateral corner
